title: 'Steps' Retells Cinderella From the Stepsisters' Side
summary:
Netflix's new animated film "Steps" gives the Cinderella story a fresh twist. This time, the spotlight falls not on Cinderella but on her stepsisters. The film follows in the footsteps of "Shrek" and "Wicked", which also retold familiar fairy tales from a so-called villain's point of view.

The story centers on Lilith, voiced by Ali Wong, an angsty teen with a goth look, and her younger sister Margot, voiced by Stephanie Hsu. The sisters arrived in the kingdom of Alouette a decade earlier, when their mother, a traveling seamstress, fell for Cinderella's father. A rift grew between the girls when Cinderella, afraid of being left out, did not stand up for them. Now Lilith resents Cinderella's picture-perfect personality, and the film follows the stepsisters as they try to mend their bond through a series of magical adventures.

Cinderella is voiced by Amanda Seyfried, who also gets to sing in the film. The new villain of the piece is Priscilla, voiced by Nikki Glaser, a self-centered girl jealous of anyone who gets more attention than her. Her henchman Roderick, voiced by Peter Dinklage, is one of the film's most memorable characters.

The review finds the film consistently funny, with clever one-liners that poke fun at fairytale tropes, and a brightly colored kingdom in gorgeous pastel shades. But the story is also crowded and hard to follow, with chases, a romance for Lilith and even time travel. One delightful moment comes when Margot turns into a pudgy frog, her hair buns becoming the frog's eyes. The film may entertain young viewers, the review says, but it does not quite become a classic.
why_it_matters: Stories told from another character's side show that there can be more than one way to see the same events, which matters when we judge people in real life too.

background_read: Cinderella is a well-known fairy tale about a kind girl who is treated badly at home and then gets to go to a ball.
In the old tale, her stepsisters are usually the mean characters who make her life hard.
This film turns the tale around and tells the story from the stepsisters' side, so viewers see their feelings and their friendship instead.
Films like this are made by drawing or building the pictures on computers, and actors record the voices for the characters.
